question.problem: Riding his electric bike, Matt can go $\frac{1}{2}$ of a mile in $\frac{3}{4}$  minutes. What is the unit rate of miles covered per minute?
question.worked_solution:
To compute the unit rate of miles per minute, we divide the number of miles, $\frac{1}{2},$ by the number of minutes, $\frac{3}{4}$, as follows: 

$$
\frac{1}{2}÷\frac{3}{4}
$$

Dividing a fraction by another fraction is equivalent to multiplying the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}÷\frac{3}{4} & =\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{1\times 4}{2\times 3} \\  & =\frac{2\times 2}{2\times 3} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{2}\times 2}{\cancel{2}\times 3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the unit rate is $\frac{2}{3}$ miles per minute.
